chunks: And by this same chain, from Fadala, from Jamil, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no wudu required for kissing, nor for touching the private parts, nor for bodily contact."
As for what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever touches a dog must perform wudu."
He means by it the washing of the two hands, as we have explained previously — that is what indicates it.

key_terms.الْقُبْلَةِ: kissing; physical contact that does not invalidate wudu
key_terms.الْمُلَامَسَةِ: bodily contact/touching; the Quranic term whose jurisprudential import this hadith clarifies
key_terms.غَسْلَ الْيَدَيْنِ: washing of the two hands (as distinct from full wudu)

ai.seo_question: Does kissing or touching the private parts invalidate wudu according to Shia hadith from the Imams?
ai.summary: These two hadiths address which acts of physical contact necessitate wudu. The first, from Imam al-Baqir (AS) via Zurara, categorically negates any wudu obligation for kissing, touching the private parts, or bodily contact — a ruling directly relevant to the Quranic term al-mulammasa (4:43). The second, from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), commands wudu after touching a dog, which Shaykh al-Tusi interprets as meaning only the washing of the two hands, not a full ritual ablution.
